Definition: a blow (figuratively, infliction); also (by implication) a spot (concretely, a leprous person or dress)
BiblicalUsage: On the plague in the skin the priest looks and pronounces it clean or unclean, and he goes outside the camp to see whether the leper is healed. The law carries hard matters of judgment to the priests, and Solomon prays that when pestilence comes the LORD would hear from heaven.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the plague is the picture of sin laid bare: it is looked at, named, and carried outside the camp, and only the priest can declare it clean. My sin is the same — it must be seen, named, and cleansed by Another.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
